items.stem: The pattern of the magnetic field produced inside a current carrying solenoid is
items.answer: (a) The magnetic field is nearly uniform inside the solenoid, hence the field lines are parallel straight lines inside the solenoid. The magnetic field produced inside a solenoid depends on the number of turns, the current and the nature of the material of the solenoid. Thus (a) is the correct option.

items.stem: The magnetic field inside a long straight current carrying solenoid:

options.label: A
options.text: is zero

options.label: B
options.text: decreases as we move towards its end.

options.label: C
options.text: increases as we move towards its end

options.label: D
options.text: is same at all points.

items.answer: (d) The magnetic field inside a long straight current-carrying solenoid is uniform, which is represented by parallel lines. Hence, the magnetic field inside a long straight solenoid carrying current is the same at all points. Thus option (d) is the correct option.

items.stem: Which of the following statement is not correct about the magnetic field?

options.label: A
options.text: Magnetic field lines form a continuous closed curve.

options.label: B
options.text: Magnetic field line do not intersect each other.

options.label: C
options.text: Direction of tangent at any point on the magnetic field line curve gives the direction of magnetic field at that point.

items.answer: (d) Outside the magnet, magnetic field lines go from South to North pole of the magnet. This is the statement that is not correct: outside the magnet the field lines run from the north pole to the south pole.

items.stem: The strength of magnetic field around a current carrying conductor is

options.label: A
options.text: inversely proportional to the current but directly proportional to the square of the distance from wire.

options.label: B
options.text: directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from wire.

options.label: C

items.stem: A circular loop placed in a plane perpendicular to the plane of paper carries a current when the key is ON. The current as seen from points A and B (in the plane of paper and on the axis of the coil) is anti-clockwise and clockwise respectively. The magnetic field lines point from B to A. The N-pole of the resultant magnet is on the face close to

options.label: A
options.text: A

options.label: B
options.text: B

options.label: C
options.text: A if the current is small, and B if the current is large

options.label: D
options.text: B if the current is small and A if the current is large.

items.answer: (a) A. The misconception is that magnetic field lines point from the north pole to the south pole; in fact they emerge out of the north pole and enter into the south pole. Since the field lines point from B to A, the N-pole is on the face close to A.

Column IColumn II

items.stem:
Two wires each carrying a steady current I are shown in four configurations in Column I. Some of the resulting effects are described in Column II. Match the statements in Column I with the statements in column II. (The current configurations of Column I are shown in the attached figure.)
Column IColumn II
(A)Point P is situated midway between the wires.(p)The magnetic fields (B) at P due to the currents in the wires are in the same direction.
(B)Point P is situated at the mid-point of the line joining the centres of the circular wires, which have same radii.(q)The magnetic fields (B) at P due to the currents in the wires are in opposite directions.
(C)Point P is situated at the mid-point of the line joining the centers of the circular wires, which have same radii.(r)There is no magnetic field at P.
(D)Point P is situated at the common center of the wires.(s)The wires repel each other.

options.label: A
options.text: A-p, r; B-r, s; C-q, s; D-s

options.label: B
options.text: A-s; B-p; C-q; D-r

options.label: C
options.text: A-q, r; B-p; C-q, r; D-q, s

options.label: D
options.text: A-q, s; B-q, r; C-s; D-s

items.answer: (c) A-q, r; B-p; C-q, r; D-q, s. A: the magnetic field at P due to the current flowing in AB is perpendicular to the plane of the paper acting vertically downward, and the field at P due to the current in CD is perpendicular to the plane of the paper acting vertically upwards, so q is correct; as P is the mid-point the two fields cancel each other, so r is also correct. B-p: the magnetic field at P due to the current in loop A is along the axial line towards the right and the field at P due to the current in loop B is also along the axial line towards the right. C-q, r: the magnetic field at P due to the current in loop A is equal and opposite to that due to the current in loop B. D-q, s: the field at P due to the current in loop A is perpendicular to the plane of the paper directed vertically upwards while that due to loop B is directed vertically downward; since the currents are in opposite directions the wires repel each other.

items.stem: Assertion (A): The magnetic field is stronger at a point which is nearer to the conductor and goes on decreasing on moving away from the conductor. Reason (R): The magnetic field B produced by a straight current carrying wire is inversely proportional to the distance from the wire.

options.label: A

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). The magnitude of the magnetic field is (i) directly proportional to the current I passing through the wire and (ii) inversely proportional to the distance r from the wire. Therefore the magnetic field is stronger at a point nearer to the conductor and goes on decreasing on moving away from the conductor.

items.answer: (b) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A). The metallic body of the electrical appliance is connected to the third pin which is connected to the earth. This is a safety precaution and avoids eventual electric shock: the extra charge flowing through the metallic body is passed to the earth and shocks are avoided. There is nothing such as reducing the heating of connecting wires by three pin connections.
